status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should respect the rule of law, human rights and democratic and human-centred values throughout the AI lifecycle, including non-discrimination, equality, freedom, dignity, individual autonomy, privacy and data protection, diversity, fairness, social justice and internationally recognised labour rights.
review.reason_for_change: The disputed AI-related elimination of unionised roles makes labour rights relevant to the AI deployment. The complete operative technology clause, its AI-causation trigger and the grievance resolution are not available. The union alleges an avoided consultation route; the hospital disputes the account. These sources do not resolve whether the rights requirement held.

conclusion_change.previous: The potential governance failure is an avoided negotiated consultation route if AI-caused staffing reduction triggered it. The public evidence establishes a grievance and displaced roles, but not the complete operative clause, agreed scope or resolution of whether that conditional trigger occurred. It does not establish an automated clinical decision or patient injury. The alleged negotiated meeting route remains conditional on the operative clause and AI-causation trigger, both disputed. The unresolved contractual duty has no matching admitted canonical requirement; it is not replaced with a generic standards duty. Workforce loss does not establish automated clinical authority or patient harm, and the conflicting effective dates remain bounded.
